newsitem.title: UK: LME copper surges on pre-market, zinc above $1,300.
newsitem.headline: LME copper surges on pre-market, zinc above $1,300.

text.p: Copper burst through nearby resistance on Monday morning on commission house and Far Eastern buying, and was primed to challenge the psychological $2,400 per tonne level in later ring trading, traders said.
"At these levels it looks quite encouraging," said one.
Three months copper was last at $2,387, up $19 from Friday's afternoon kerb close.
Copper's late bout of strength on Friday afternoon had surprised some in the market and a large portion of the buying so far on Monday was short covering, he added.
Volumes were not substantial, however, and many were not convinced that copper could make much progress over $2,400 to attack further resistance at $2,409 and $2,440.
"People are a little bit wary, sceptical," a trader said.
Another trader said he had heard conflicting talk regarding the physical market, with some people saying scrap was tight and others saying physical material was well offered.
The premium of cash over three months surged about $10 to $65/70.
Short covering on zinc in the wake of copper's strength sent it nudging above $1,300 in pre-market dealing, with prices last indicated at $1,302/3 versus a $1,297 Friday close.
Last Thursday's high of $1,307 was expected to provide resistance on any further upside moves, while $1,286 was important trendline support, said chartist Harry Creates of broker AMT.
Aluminium was encouraged by from the firmer tone in the market, breaking above $1,669, the high of last Thursday and Friday.
It was last indicated at $1,671/74, up from $1,657 on Friday.
Analysts said aluminium needed more time to consolidate before resuming the uptrend. Support was pegged at $1,637 and after $1,669, resistance was seen at $1,680.
Other metals saw little business but nickel was marked up slightly with copper to be last indicated at $7,970/90, up from $7,955 on Friday.
"On the upside there is heavy resistance up to $8,175 to overcome," said Creates.
Lead and tin were little changed at $690/$692 versus Friday's $692 and $5,925/45 compared with $5,925.
